answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create urgent pressure, but the 94% volume buffer leaves no room for switching risk. Memory_c6 demonstrates that multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing that could absorb the 18% target without scope cuts. Memory_c4 shows benchmarking moves incumbents on both price and terms. Rather than renew passively (c1) or switch to the low-cost vendor (c2—which worked before but at a time with higher buffers), aggressive renegotiation with the incumbent leverages their proven reliability and integration stability while forcing cost reduction. The constraint is time; this requires immediate escalation to complete benchmarking and negotiation within 14 days. If negotiation fails, deferral past quarter-end (c5 pattern) becomes the fallback, though that creates month-to-month risk at 94% utilization. Verification targets confirm the math on volume pricing upside and the precedent for successful margin recovery.
